rationale: B wins because it does more strategic work with the same ugly facts: it turns the MOU and the no-orbit weakness into reporter-shaped angles, especially "Minutes" is a claim, not a capability, until something is in orbit." A is cleaner, but its "Can satellites cut wildfire detection from hours to minutes?" category angle is safer and also sneaks in an unsupported "hours" baseline. B needs a fact-check broom, but it gives the founder more usable routes than A's founder/funding/category trio.
gaps_in_A: "Can satellites cut wildfire detection from hours to minutes?" invents the "hours" baseline; the update only says Helio aims to alert agencies faster than current systems and within minutes.
A misses the strongest non-funding protagonist: the unnamed state fire agency MOU. It treats the agency mostly as proof for the category angle instead of testing an agency-procurement story.
"launch-cadence and rocket discipline from SpaceX plus Earth-observation constellation experience from Planet Labs" leans on biography as capability before confirming the founders' actual roles.
The next step jumps to "journalist-fit-check" before resolving the fatal proof holes: agency name, fund name, launch milestone, and measured detection claim.
gaps_in_B: "Ex-SpaceX and Planet Labs engineers" invents "engineers"; the facts only say the founders are ex-SpaceX and ex-Planet Labs.
"agencies are signing before the hardware exists" turns one unnamed state-agency MOU into a plural trend. That is exactly how a thin fact gets dressed up for trouble.
"customer-story" overstates the MOU. No revenue, named customer, purchase intent, or operational use was disclosed.
"The prevailing belief this cuts against is real and currently loud" manufactures a current discourse without supplied evidence. Make that proof, not copy.
